title: “Venerable sirs, for one who has abandoned lust for form, abandoned desire, abandoned love, abandoned thirst, abandoned passion, abandoned craving — when that form changes…
content: “Venerable sirs, for one who has abandoned lust for form, abandoned desire, abandoned love, abandoned thirst, abandoned passion, abandoned craving — when that form changes and alters, no sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, or despair arise. For feeling … perception … formations … For one who has abandoned lust for consciousness, abandoned desire, abandoned love, abandoned thirst, abandoned passion, abandoned craving — when that consciousness changes and alters, no sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, or despair arise. Seeing this benefit, venerable sirs, our Teacher speaks of the subduing of desire and lust for form … for feeling … for perception … for formations; our Teacher speaks of the subduing of desire and lust for consciousness. And because one attains and dwells in wholesome states, living at ease in this very life, without obstruction, without distress, without fever, and at the breakup of the body, after death, one will be reborn in a good destination. Therefore, this is the accomplishment of wholesome states praised by the Blessed One.”

title: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms,…
content: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — then, monks, this is called a monk who has gone into Māra’s domain, who has come under Māra’s control. Māra’s net has surrounded him. Bound by Māra, he is subject to the Evil One’s will … Monks, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk delights in those phenomena, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — then, monks, this is called a monk who has gone into Māra’s domain, who has come under Māra’s control. Māra’s net has surrounded him. Bound by Māra, he is subject to the Evil One’s will.”

title: “Monks, then I thought: ‘This Dhamma I have attained is deep, hard to see, hard to realize, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of mere logic,…
content: “Monks, then I thought: ‘This Dhamma I have attained is deep, hard to see, hard to realize, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of mere logic, subtle, to be understood only by the wise. But this generation delights in sensual pleasures, is devoted to sensual pleasures, is fond of sensual pleasures. For a generation that delights, is devoted, and is fond of sensual pleasures, it is hard to see this principle of specific conditionality (dependent origination); it is also hard to see the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all substrates, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.’”

title: “Monks, one who delights in forms delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in…
content: “Monks, one who delights in forms delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who delights in sounds … in odors … in tastes … in touches … One who delights in phenomena delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. One who does not delight in forms, monks, does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering. One who does not delight in sounds … odors … tastes … touches … One who does not delight in phenomena does not delight in suffering. One who does not delight in suffering, I say, is freed from suffering.”

title: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, they engage in misconduct of body,…
content: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, they engage in misconduct of body, misconduct of speech, misconduct of mind. Having engaged in misconduct of body, speech, and mind, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Monks, such is the peril of sensuality, leading to future suffering, a mass of suffering, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis – simply because of sensuality.”

title: … Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One: Life is swept along, Short is the lifespan…
content:
… Standing to one side, that deity recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
Life is swept along,
Short is the lifespan —
To old age we are led,
There is no stopping place.
Seeing this danger in death,
Do meritorious deeds
That bring true happiness.

(The Blessed One):
Life is swept along,
Short is the lifespan —
To old age we are led,
There is no stopping place.
Seeing this danger in death,
Seeking peace, abandon worldly hopes.

title: Elder Sabbhakāma: This two-footed creature, Impure and foul-smelling, Full of various corpses — From it, fluid oozes. With deer, use a trap; with fish, a…
content:
Elder Sabbhakāma:

This two-footed creature,
Impure and foul-smelling,
Full of various corpses —
From it, fluid oozes.

With deer, use a trap; with fish, a hook;
With monkeys, a pit;
Thus worldlings are caught.

Forms, sounds, tastes, smells, touches —
Agreeable and pleasing —
These five strands of sensual pleasure
Are known in female form.

Worldlings, with mind infatuated,
Run after enjoying female form.
The terrifying cemetery increases,
Storing up renewed existence.

One who avoids female form
As a foot avoids a snake’s head —
That mindful one overcomes
The world’s poisoner.

Seeing the danger in sensual pleasures,
Security in renunciation,
Having escaped all sensual pleasures,
I have attained the destruction of defilements.

title: Forms, sounds, tastes, odors, touches, And all phenomena — Desirable, delightful, agreeable — Thus they are called. Devas and humans in the world, Regarding them…
content:
Forms, sounds, tastes, odors, touches,
And all phenomena —
Desirable, delightful, agreeable —
Thus they are called.

Devas and humans in the world,
Regarding them as delightful —
Where they cease and fade away,
Devas and humans see suffering.

The noble one sees as ease
When identity view is destroyed —
The noble one sees as opposite
All the views of the world.

What others call pleasure,
The noble call suffering.
What others call suffering,
The noble know as pleasure.

See the Dhamma, hard to comprehend,
Where the ignorant are bewildered —
Darkness for the blind,
Obscurity for those who cannot see.

For the good person with open eyes,
Light is clearly seen —
Living close, they know clearly,
Skilled in the great Dhamma.

Overcome by the thirst of birth,
Swept away by the current of existence,
Subject to Māra’s control —
They do not awaken to this Dhamma.

Apart from the noble ones, no one
Awakens to this path —
The path leading to Nibbāna,
With perfect wisdom, free from defilements.

title: “But this body, Aggivessana, is material, composed of the four great elements, born of father and mother, nourished with rice and porridge, impermanent, subject to…
content: “But this body, Aggivessana, is material, composed of the four great elements, born of father and mother, nourished with rice and porridge, impermanent, subject to rubbing, pressing, breaking, disintegration, dissolution. It should be contemplated as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease, as a boil, as a dart, as misery, as an affliction, as alien, as disintegrating, as empty, as not-self. When he contemplates this body as impermanent, as suffering, as a disease … as not-self, then bodily desire, bodily fondness, bodily subjection are abandoned.”

title: Then Māra, having transformed himself into a brahmin with a large topknot, wearing an antelope skin, old, bent like a rafter, breathing heavily, carrying a…
content:
Then Māra, having transformed himself into a brahmin with a large topknot, wearing an antelope skin, old, bent like a rafter, breathing heavily, carrying a udumbara staff, approached those monks. Having approached, he said to them:
- “Venerable sirs, you have gone forth too young, in the prime of youth, with black hair, in the bloom of youth, at the early stage of life, without having enjoyed sensual pleasures. Venerable sirs, enjoy human sensual pleasures. Do not abandon the present to chase after what is subject to time.”

- “Brahmin, we do not abandon the present to chase after what is subject to time. And, brahmin, we abandon what is subject to time to chase after the present. The Blessed One has said that sensual pleasures are subject to time, of great suffering, of great despair — the peril in them is even greater. This Dhamma is visible here and now, not subject to time, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”
